task_instance: Use the skill's bundled health_query.py against an Apple Health SQLite database to produce a daily health summary (steps, active calories, heart rate avg/min/max, exercise minutes, distance, activity rings) and exercise the other query modes (weekly trends, sleep analysis, latest vitals, activity rings, workout history, custom SQL) in all four output formats (markdown, json, fhir, ascii).
evidence: Pre-installed python3 3.13.17 with the sqlite3 module (3.45.1) is available; no network, no installs, no connectors used. The skill's required file scripts/health_query.py and references/schema.md + fhir_mappings.md are present next to SKILL.md. The database ~/data/health.db is user-supplied input data and does not exist, so I created a small realistic sample as INPUT (not a replacement of any skill file): make_sample.py builds health_sample.db following references/schema.md exactly (tables health_records=294 rows, workouts=7, sleep_sessions=56, activity_summaries=14; 14 days of data ending today, with a deliberate iPhone step duplicate to test the script's Watch-only dedup). I copied the unmodified skill script into the work dir and made one minimal, non-functional adaptation: DB_PATH now reads an optional HEALTH_DB env var (falling back to ~/data/health.db) so it can point at the sample DB, since I may not write outside the work directory. Ran the script's own logic in every mode: `daily --date 2026-10-31` (markdown and ascii) returned steps=6704 (correctly excluding the iPhone duplicate of 4000, proving the dedup query ran), active_calories=480.1, heart_rate avg 71.8/min 54/max 119, plus a rendered activity-ring bar chart; `vitals --format fhir` produced a valid FHIR R4 Bundle of Observation resources with correct LOINC codes (Heart rate 8867-4, etc.); `sleep --days 7` returned 8 nights with avg 6.3h; `weekly --weeks 2` returned per-week avg steps/resting HR/exercise min/workout counts; `workouts --days 14 --type Running` returned 7 running sessions with duration/distance/calories and a by-type summary; `activity --days 14` returned ring completion summary; and a custom `query` ran arbitrary SQL. Saved a markdown deliverable to daily_report.md (435 bytes). The only non-functional artifacts are the FHIR system fields showing [url-1]/[url-2]/[url-3], which are placeholder substitutions in the skill copy, not errors. Files produced: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r161/{health_sample.db, make_sample.py, health_query.py, daily_report.md, result.json}.
